title: Machine learning predicts epileptogenic foci and surgical outcomes in tuberous sclerosis
summary: On 665 cortical foci (161 epileptogenic) from three epilepsy centers, a super-learner ensemble of clinical and radiomic features reached AUCs of 0.92 in a prospective cohort and 0.91 and 0.87 in two retrospective cohorts. Models also predicted 1-, 3- and 5-year surgical outcomes with AUCs of 0.93, 0.91 and 0.92, and junior clinician accuracy rose from 0.61 to 0.78 with the tool. The data are focus-level in a rare disease with few patients, and the web tool has no external validation.
ai_technology: Nineteen machine learning models and three ensembles (voting, averaging, super-learner) on clinical and radiomic features of CT, MRI and FDG-PET

evidence.tested: Prospective cohort and two retrospective cohorts across three centers with surgical follow-up; classified as retrospective or benchmark because model derivation used retrospective data.
evidence.unknown: Patient-level performance, external validation of the web tool and effect on surgical decisions; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranks cortical foci as epileptogenic or not and forecasts post-surgical seizure outcome.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
